definition: Sense Networks is a New York City based company with a focus on applications that analyze big data from mobile phones, carrier networks, and taxicabs, particularly by using machine learning technology to make sense of large amounts of location (latitude/longitude) data.
details: In 2009, Sense was named one of "The 25 Most Intriguing Startups in the World" by Bloomberg Businessweek and was called "The Next Google" on the cover of Newsweek. In 2014, Sense Networks was acquired by YP, "the local search and advertising company owned by Cerberus Capital Management and AT&T." It was subsequently sold off to Verve in 2017

explainer.lead: Sense Networks was a New York City company focused on applications that analyse big data from mobile phones, carrier networks and taxicabs. It mattered as an early commercial effort to make sense of large-scale location data with machine learning.

tiers.eli5: It was a company that used machine learning to find patterns in where lots of people and taxis go.
tiers.practitioner: Its work centred on large amounts of latitude/longitude data from phones, carriers and cabs. A pitfall for such location analytics is that results depend heavily on how location data is collected and sampled.
tiers.paperLevel: A company applying machine learning to large volumes of latitude/longitude location data from mobile phones, carrier networks and taxicabs.

explainer.example: Analysing taxi and phone location traces to reveal patterns in how people move through a city.
